pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sacred plant belongs to Buddhist tradition because of the Buddha's enlightenment? (1 mark)
   A. Ber tree
   B. Sal tree
   C. Bodhi tree
   D. Tulsi

2. Which is a good way to collect free water for the home? (1 mark)
   A. Taking water from a neighbour
   B. Buying bottled water only
   C. Collecting rainwater from a roof
   D. Digging a hole in the road

3. Where do Hindu families often grow Tulsi? (1 mark)
   A. Under the roof
   B. Only in a river
   C. In the kitchen fire
   D. In a pot or raised stand in the courtyard

4. In the seed activity, what happens to the seeds that get no water? (1 mark)
   A. They turn into stones
   B. They grow tall fast
   C. They do not grow
   D. They turn blue

5. Which is a role of trees and plants? (1 mark)
   A. They make the sun set
   B. They dry up rivers
   C. They stop rain forever
   D. They give oxygen and shade

6. Why is water needed by all living things? (1 mark)
   A. It is always warm
   B. Life cannot continue without it
   C. It hides the sun
   D. It makes things noisy

7. Which of these is NOT one of the five elements? (1 mark)
   A. Prithvi
   B. Metal
   C. Agni
   D. Vayu

8. What should you do when you join a religious activity of another faith? (1 mark)
   A. Listen carefully and behave politely
   B. Make noise
   C. Refuse to sit
   D. Laugh at it

9. What is a Tirthankar in Jainism? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. A teacher who shows the path across the river of life
   C. A king
   D. A temple

10. In the story of the swan, who shot the swan? (1 mark)
   A. Siddhartha
   B. Devadatta
   C. Prahlad
   D. Suddhodana

11. What does Ahimsa mean? (1 mark)
   A. Eating late
   B. Not hurting any living being
   C. Telling stories
   D. Paying taxes

12. How did Prahlad react when his father was angry? (1 mark)
   A. He became cruel
   B. He stayed calm and kept his faith
   C. He gave up praying
   D. He ran away forever

13. Whom did Ram marry in the Bal Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Saraswati
   B. Ganga
   C. Sita
   D. Kaikeyi

14. Which of these is one of the six directions in the Sigalovada Sutta? (1 mark)
   A. Kings
   B. Strangers
   C. Rivers
   D. Teachers

15. What did Bharat place on the throne? (1 mark)
   A. A crown
   B. Ram's sandals (paduka)
   C. A lamp
   D. A book

16. Which quality of Ram is taught in the Bal Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Pride
   B. Respect for parents and teachers
   C. Laziness
   D. Cruelty

17. Which of these were sons of King Dasharatha? (1 mark)
   A. Ram, Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughna
   B. Ram, Sigala, Bharat and Shibi
   C. Lakshman, Devadatta, Ram and Bharat
   D. Prahlad, Ram and Jetha

18. Which is a bad habit during prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Sitting still
   B. Laughing or talking
   C. Folding hands
   D. Listening

19. Which is the first line of the Gayatri Mantra? (1 mark)
   A. Ya Kundendu Tushara
   B. Om Namah Shivaya
   C. Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva
   D. Om Bhur Bhuvah Svah

20. How can you show a Mandir in a drawing? (1 mark)
   A. A circle only
   B. A zigzag line
   C. A rectangle hall with a pointed spire
   D. A river

21. Which Jain teaching means not stealing? (1 mark)
   A. Aparigraha
   B. Satya
   C. Asteya
   D. Ahimsa

22. Which best describes a person with integrity? (1 mark)
   A. Rich
   B. Loud
   C. Honest even when nobody is watching
   D. Honest only when watched

23. What does Vajra mean in Vajra Asana? (1 mark)
   A. Moon
   B. Bellows
   C. Diamond or thunderbolt
   D. Hare

24. Which is a mistake in yoga? (1 mark)
   A. Working with a teacher
   B. Breathing slowly
   C. Holding the breath for too long
   D. Stopping if unwell

25. How can children with special needs take part? (1 mark)
   A. In their own way, such as breathing slowly or seated poses
   B. Only by watching
   C. They cannot join
   D. By leaving

26. What does asana mean? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A posture or seat
   C. A prayer
   D. A river

27. Which pose is called the hare or moon pose? (1 mark)
   A. Sasankasana
   B. Vajra Asana
   C. Kapaal Bhaati
   D. Bhastrika

28. According to Hindu belief, what does the soul do after death? (1 mark)
   A. Takes a new body
   B. Ends forever
   C. Turns to stone
   D. Turns into a tree only

29. What did King Shibi offer to save the dove? (1 mark)
   A. His own flesh, weight for weight
   B. His shoes
   C. His crown
   D. His horse

30. What does Moksha mean? (1 mark)
   A. A game
   B. A song
   C. Freedom of the soul
   D. A meal

31. Paryushan Parva is a festival of which faith? (1 mark)
   A. Jainism
   B. Sikhism
   C. Buddhism
   D. Hinduism

32. What is a jagaran or vigil? (1 mark)
   A. A meal
   B. Eating a big meal
   C. Staying awake at night to pray and sing
   D. A race

33. What does fasting on Maha Shivratri show? (1 mark)
   A. Self-control
   B. Laziness
   C. Anger
   D. Greed

34. Which practice is part of Paryushan? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating
   B. Fasting
   C. Shouting
   D. Hunting

35. Which festival is a national festival? (1 mark)
   A. Maha Shivratri
   B. Paryushan Parva
   C. Vasant Panchami
   D. Madaraka Day

36. Which mistake is common about Madaraka Day? (1 mark)
   A. Knowing it is 1 June
   B. Knowing it is for patriots
   C. Thinking it is Independence Day
   D. Knowing the flag is raised

37. What does vaar mean? (1 mark)
   A. Month
   B. Year
   C. Planet
   D. Day of the week

38. What is the Indian name for Saturday? (1 mark)
   A. Shanivaar
   B. Guruvaar
   C. Ravivaar
   D. Mangalvaar

39. How many months are in the Indian traditional calendar year? (1 mark)
   A. Fifteen
   B. Ten
   C. Seven
   D. Twelve

40. Which day is linked with Venus? (1 mark)
   A. Friday
   B. Monday
   C. Sunday
   D. Wednesday

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain what we learn from the lives of any two Enlightened Beings. (4 marks)

42. Explain why the time and place of the defeat of Hiranyakashipu are special in the story. (3 marks)

43. Name two parts of a Mandir. (2 marks)

44. Explain how the school can plan a tree planting day that includes learners with special needs. (5 marks)

45. Explain how learners can include friends with special needs in yoga. (5 marks)

46. Describe the snake story of Lord Parshvanath. (3 marks)

47. Distinguish between Madaraka Day and Jamhuri Day. (3 marks)

48. Explain how children who find it hard to speak can join in prayers at assembly. (4 marks)

49. Give the date and origin of International Yoga Day. (2 marks)

50. Explain why water is important in our daily lives. (3 marks)

51. Why is Saraswati shown with a veena and a book? (2 marks)

52. Write a short composition on a festival of your choice. (5 marks)

53. State three contributions of Sri Guru Ram Das Ji. (3 marks)

54. Give three activities to learn about temples. (3 marks)

55. Explain why the Indian traditional calendar is special and how a child can use it. (5 marks)

56. State three ways of showing respect to the National flag and Anthem. (3 marks)

57. Describe what Prince Siddhartha did when a swan was hurt. (3 marks)

58. What is an asana? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Bodhi tree
   Bodhi tree is the tree of awakening.

2. C — Collecting rainwater from a roof
   Roof water can be stored in a tank or jerrican.

3. D — In a pot or raised stand in the courtyard
   The stand is called the Tulsi Vrindavan.

4. C — They do not grow
   Seeds need water to sprout.

5. D — They give oxygen and shade
   Plants clean the air and give shade.

6. B — Life cannot continue without it
   People, animals and plants all need water to live.

7. B — Metal
   The five are earth, water, fire, air and space.

8. A — Listen carefully and behave politely
   We show respect to all faiths.

9. B — A teacher who shows the path across the river of life
   Tirthankars guide people to freedom.

10. B — Devadatta
   Devadatta shot an arrow at the swan.

11. B — Not hurting any living being
   Ahimsa is non-violence in thought, word and action.

12. B — He stayed calm and kept his faith
   Prahlad kept his faith without fear.

13. C — Sita
   Ram married Sita in Mithila.

14. D — Teachers
   Parents, teachers, family, friends, workers and holy teachers.

15. B — Ram's sandals (paduka)
   Bharat ruled in Ram's name.

16. B — Respect for parents and teachers
   Ram was truthful, polite and brave.

17. A — Ram, Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughna
   These were the four brothers.

18. B — Laughing or talking
   We should be quiet and respectful.

19. D — Om Bhur Bhuvah Svah
   The Gayatri Mantra begins Om Bhur Bhuvah Svah.

20. C — A rectangle hall with a pointed spire
   A hall with a spire is a simple model.

21. C — Asteya
   Asteya is non-stealing.

22. C — Honest even when nobody is watching
   Integrity is honesty at all times.

23. C — Diamond or thunderbolt
   Vajra means diamond or thunderbolt.

24. C — Holding the breath for too long
   Never force the breath.

25. A — In their own way, such as breathing slowly or seated poses
   Everyone can take part.

26. B — A posture or seat
   An asana is a posture.

27. A — Sasankasana
   Sasankasana.

28. A — Takes a new body
   This is rebirth.

29. A — His own flesh, weight for weight
   He offered himself.

30. C — Freedom of the soul
   Moksha is the highest goal.

31. A — Jainism
   It is the main Jain festival.

32. C — Staying awake at night to pray and sing
   Devotees stay awake.

33. A — Self-control
   It teaches self-control.

34. B — Fasting
   Fasting, prayer and charity.

35. D — Madaraka Day
   It is celebrated by all Kenyans.

36. C — Thinking it is Independence Day
   Independence is 12 December.

37. D — Day of the week
   Vaar means day.

38. A — Shanivaar
   Shani is Saturn.

39. D — Twelve
   It has twelve months.

40. A — Friday
   Shukravaar.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any two, for example: from Prahlad's story that faith and honesty can defeat pride, and from Siddhartha that we must be kind to hurt animals.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each being with a correct lesson.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Narsimha was neither man nor animal, it was neither day nor night, and it happened at the doorway, neither inside nor outside, so the king's gift did not protect him.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three details.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Entrance, main hall, inner room (garbhagriha), spire (shikhara), bell (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a suitable place and get permission, prepare seedlings, tools and water, and give each child a job they can do, such as holding seedlings, filling watering cans or drawing the plants. Care for the trees afterwards.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for permission, preparing, jobs for all, inclusion of special needs, and continued care.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: They can do breathing slowly, take seated poses, help hold the chart or take photos, and be encouraged by their partners. Everyone's effort is respected.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points and 1 mark for respect.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: A man was burning a log. Parshvanath saw that a snake was inside and asked him to stop. The snake was saved, and the man learned a lesson about kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the log, 1 mark for the snake, 1 mark for the rescue or lesson.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Madaraka Day is 1 June and marks internal self-government in 1963. Jamhuri Day is 12 December and marks independence in 1963 and the republic in 1964.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each date and 1 mark for a difference.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: They can hum, listen, join the actions or be helped by friends, so nobody is left out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four sensible points.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: 21 June, chosen by the United Nations.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the date, 1 mark for the United Nations.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Water is needed for drinking and cooking, for washing and cleaning, and for growing crops and giving drinks to animals. Without it people, animals and plants cannot live.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three correct points.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: The veena stands for music and the arts and the book stands for knowledge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any well-organised composition naming the festival, when it is held, what people do, what it teaches and how you feel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for name, timing, activities, meaning, and feeling.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: He started the city of Amritsar and the Sarovar, composed hymns and the Laavan, and taught equality and service.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each contribution.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make a collage of temple pictures, map Mandirs on a sketch map or digital map, draw and colour a Mandir, visit one with permission (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: It links daily life to the sky and seasons, keeps tradition alive and fixes festival dates. A child can make a weekly plan, a decorated calendar, greeting cards or a song.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for why it is special and 3 marks for uses.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stand straight, be quiet, never let the flag touch the ground, learn and sing the anthem (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: He pulled out the arrow, nursed the swan and, when it was well, let it go free. He said that saving a life matters more than taking it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for nursing, arrow, letting go free.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: A body posture.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for posture or seat.
